title: Use custom prompts and additional parameters
text: datavana service based precomposed prompts different workflows. can override default prompt templates -pass post-processing get direct LLM answers using llm_prompt() function. Provide prompts prompt.user- prompt.system-parameters. prompts, case input data frame df, placeholder {{text}} replaced content selected abstract column. Note: previous example, used paste0() concatenate sentences. serves readability, alternatively, can provide prompt one single character string.
code: # Submit tasks results <- llm_prompt(   df, abstract,      prompt.system = paste0(     "Output a comma separated list of categories. ",     "Just the list, nothing else. ",     "The possible categories are: scifi, historical, drama, comedy, fantasy, romance"   ),      prompt.user = "{{text}}"    )   # Fetch results results <- llm_prompt(custom)

what: Adapt prompts for the existing workflow methods
title: Use custom prompts and additional parameters
text: Instead using llm_prompt()-function, can also adapt prompts used workflow-specific functions llm_summarize(), llm_code() llm_annotate(). Using technique, can leverage pre- post-processing steps Databoard service. example, providing rules, result automatically split one field category. way: hood, llm_prompt() function uses summary workflow settings simply disable result processing. prompt templates, use {{text}} placeholder define slot content data frame inserted. {{rules}} placeholder replaced markdown formatted list rules provided rules book. using rules, make sure prompt compatible expected pattern. post-processing procedure expects one line output column. whatever follows category name inserted column. enter line breaks prompt, use escape sequence \n.
code:
results <- llm_summarize(   movies, abstract, rules,       options = list(       prompts = list(         system = paste0(           "You are an expert in content analysis. Be precise and concise.",           "Use the codebook provided to decide for each category, ",           "whether the given text falls into the category. ",                      "Return one line for each category. ",           "Each returned line must start with the category name ",            "followed by a colon ':' and then followed by one of the codes ",                      "'5' if the category applies fully, ",           "'4' if the category mostly applies, ",           "'3' if the category partially applies, ",            "'2' if the category mostly does not apply, ",           "'1' if the category does not apply at all. ",                       "Return only the lines for each category - ",           "nothing else, no introduction, no explanation, no disclaimer!
",                      "# Rules:
 {{rules}}
"         ),         user = "{{text}}"      )    ) )  results <- llm_summarize(results)

title: Use custom prompts and additional parameters
text: workflows can return multiple values per case, example coding text multiple categories summarizing text multiple rules. llm_code() exposes explicit mode argument. controls coding result structured: single (default): return single best-matching category per case. multi: return one value per category, 2 means category strongly applies, 1 means applies, 0 means apply. llm_summarize() method uses idea internally, switches automatically: rules returns one result per rule, otherwise returns single summary per case. typical use case multi-mode extracting information movie’s year, topic main character’s name. Example:
code: # Single mode (default)  results <- llm_code(df, abstract, rules, mode = "single") results <- llm_code(results)  # Multi mode  results <- llm_code(df, abstract, rules, mode = "multi") results <- llm_code(results) rules <- tibble::tribble(   ~category,  ~description,                                  ~example,   "figure",   "The names of the main characters in the movie", "John Doe",   "gender",   "The gender of the main characters",             "male" )  results <- llm_summarize(df, abstract, rules) results <- llm_summarize(results)

title: Use custom prompts and additional parameters
text: workflow wrappers forward model-related settings via options list. common ones : model: choose LLM model use. temperature: control deterministic varied answer . See databoard API documentation complete list available options values. set options, server defaults used. example:
code: results <- llm_code(   df, abstract, rules,       options = list(     model = 'mistral-small',     temperature = "0.2"   ) )  results <- llm_code(results)

Firstly, submit tasks let service work. Secondly, retrieve results. R package wraps main functions service: llm_summarize() used condense text shorter paragraphs even single words. provide categories, one summary keyword returned category. llm_code() assigns predefined categories text. Provide codebook category names, descriptions, optionally examples. Depending settings, workflow return one multiple matching categories. llm_annotate() adds -text annotations, example, extract person place names. According rule set, matching text segments enclosed XML tags. predefined methods based pre-composed prompt templates include pre- post-processing steps aligned workflow. can customize prompts several options exposed service. gain full flexibility, use custom prompts -pass processing steps: llm_prompt() fetches LLM answers using prompt templates.

text: example dataframe movies column review features lengthy reviews movies’ plots. summarize shorter paragraphs, use llm_summarize() pass data frame name column containing review text. Within RStudio, inspect results object see answers.
code: # Submit the tasks to the Databoard queue results <- llm_summarize(df, review)  # Once you submitted the tasks, call the same method with # the resulting data frame as the first parameter. # Task results that are ready will be added by each call. # The  wait-parameter defines how many seconds to wait at maximum for each case to finish. results <- llm_summarize(results, wait = 10)

what: Using the service to categorize text
title: Getting started with the databoard
text: Use llm_code() function categorize text. function expects three parameters: data frame content want analyze name column containing text anlyzed codebook defining coding rules data frame codebook data frame needs contain three columns: category: categories want code description: description category example: optionally, category, provide matching examples can, example, define directly R using tribble() function prepare load csv excel file common tidyverse functions. implemented example codebook can used playing example movies dataset: data rules, let LLM categorize text: movies fall multiple categories? Try ! Set mode-parameter “multi” obtain value 0 2 category:
code: # Rule examples rules <- tibble::tribble(   ~category,  ~description,                                                               ~example,   "History",  "Movies based on real events or people from the past.",                     "Schindler’s List, Braveheart",   "Scifi",    "Stories about futuristic science, technology, space, or alien life.",      "Interstellar, Blade Runner",   "Musical",  "Films where characters sing and dance as part of the story.",              "The Greatest Showman, Mamma Mia",   "Fantasy",  "Movies featuring magical or supernatural elements and imaginary worlds.",  "Pan’s Labyrinth, Harry Potter",   "Comedy",   "Films made to entertain and make the audience laugh.",                     "Mean Girls, The Hangover",   "Drama",    "Serious stories focused on relationships, and character development.",     "Forrest Gump, A Beautiful Mind" ) # Submit results <- llm_code(df, abstract, rules)  # Keep calling until all tasks are finished. results <- llm_code(results)  # Inspect result count(results, llm_result) # Submit results <- llm_code(df, abstract, rules, mode="multi")  # Keep calling until all tasks are finished. results <- llm_code(results)

what: Using the service to annotate text

text: Use llm_annotate() extract annotate text spans according rules. rules object mandatory submit mode must provide three columns: category: used value attribute annotation description: used identify text segments example: comma-separated example segments match rule result contains matching text segment wrapped XML-tags. addition, find llm_annos column containing data frame extracted segments case. Unnest get simple data frame:
code: anno_rules <- tibble::tribble(   ~category, ~description, ~example,   "PERSON", "Names of people", "John Doe, Jane Roe",   "PLACE", "Names of places", "Berlin, New York" )  # Submit results <- llm_annotate(df, abstract, anno_rules)  # Fetch pending tasks results <- llm_annotate(results) segments <- results |>    select(id, name, llm_annos) |>    tidyr::unnest(llm_annos)

what: How to use the databoard package?
title: Automated Content Coding with Large Language Models
text: service provides three main functions: code text summarize text annotate text See introduction vignette examples.
code: library(tidyverse)  # Get example data df <- databoard::movies  # Define coding rules rules <- tibble::tribble(   ~category,  ~description,                                                               ~example,   "History",  "Movies based on real events or people from the past.",                     "Schindler’s List, Braveheart",   "Scifi",    "Stories about futuristic science, technology, space, or alien life.",      "Interstellar, Blade Runner",   "Musical",  "Films where characters sing and dance as part of the story.",              "The Greatest Showman, Mamma Mia",   "Fantasy",  "Movies featuring magical or supernatural elements and imaginary worlds.",  "Pan’s Labyrinth, Harry Potter",   "Comedy",   "Films made to entertain and make the audience laugh.",                     "Mean Girls, The Hangover",   "Drama",    "Serious stories focused on relationships, and character development.",     "Forrest Gump, A Beautiful Mind" )  write_rds(rules,"data/genres.rda")  # Submit to the databoard service results <- llm_code(movies, abstract, rules)  # Once you submitted your tasks,  # call the same method with  your data frame as the first parameter. # Task results that are ready will be added. # Keep calling until all tasks are finished. results <- llm_code(results)  # Inspect result results |>    count(llm_result)
